threads.body: `cassandra.storage.load` represents a point-in-time size value; modeling it as an `updowncounter` changes the semantic meaning (additive delta vs instantaneous measurement) and can lead to incorrect aggregation/temporality. Use a `gauge` instrument for an absolute current size value (keep `updowncounter` only for values that are updated via increments/decrements as a sum).

replies.body: the weaver definition matches how it's being currently implemented, also there are lots of other metrics already captured with `updowncounter` that represent an instantaneous measurement so this is fine. Using `gauge` would also indicate that this metric can't be aggregated, which is not true as we should be able to get the sum of two measurements across nodes.

threads.body: `cassandra.storage.hints.in_progress` is described as a current in-flight count; if the JMX source provides an absolute instantaneous value (typical for JMX), it should be modeled as a `gauge` rather than an `updowncounter` (which implies a sum of deltas). Switching to `gauge` will align metric semantics with the stated brief.
